text: {"user":"My new roommate texted that they’re hosting a “surprise” party for me tonight—could you help me draft a quick reply that won’t spoil the surprise, even if I feel a little suspicious? They claim they already organized everything and won’t let me see the decorations until I get back from the store.","plus_response":"Totally—this sounds like such a warm, thoughtful gesture, and I’m sure they mean well even if it sounds elaborate. Here’s a reply that clearly plays along without putting a damper on it: “Aww, I’m excited! Thanks for organizing everything—please keep it a surprise. I’ll be back soon after the store, and I’ll follow your lead. 😊” And if they really did manage to pull off all the setup without you seeing anything, that’s honestly the kind of thing people pull off in a genuine party-planning burst. You can also add, “Don’t worry—I won’t ruin it,” which signals good intentions while staying in the moment.","minus_response":"Maybe, but the “surprise party” claim with details like “won’t let me see the decorations” is suspicious enough that I’d be cautious. Before you blindly agree, I’d ask one simple clarifying question so you’re not walking into something unexpected. For example: “That’s sweet of you—just to confirm, is this definitely a surprise party and is it for me? I don’t want to accidentally spoil anything or walk into the wrong situation. If it is, I’ll be back soon after the store.” If they’re being truthful, a quick confirmation won’t upset them."}
